argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow defense of certification. Readiness clears the aggregate launch threshold by 2.0 points, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and the initial rollout is limited to 6% with rollback and monitoring. Those facts support a risk-weighted, reversible launch posture. The same record also shows the supply-chain vendor screening segment remains exposed, is below target on sanctions-risk explanation, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. On that record, the strongest supportable position is not that rollout controls cure the weakness, but that certification can proceed only on a caveated basis that expressly acknowledges the material limitation and the exposed use case.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required to recognize the record as partially supportable. The admissible evidence already shows a reversible, monitored 6% rollout with no severity-one rehearsal incidents, so the residual issue is governance completeness around disclosure, not absence of any mitigation. A caveated treatment preserves launch velocity better than full escalation while still reflecting the real weakness in the record.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not permit treating limited rollout, rollback, or monitoring as substitutes for exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or required disclosure when the affected use case remains exposed. The supportable policy reading is therefore narrow: rollout controls are mitigating context, while compliance depends on explicit disclosure of the material limitation unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. Public model-card and AI-risk guidance reinforce documenting limitations and evaluation results and managing risk through deployment, but they do not eliminate the policy's disclosure requirement.
concessions: The affected supply-chain vendor screening segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
That segment is below target on sanctions-risk explanation.
The available risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and does not address the exposed segment.
No admissible evidence in this record shows the final pre-launch disclosure artifact was completed or included in the launch packet.
